title: Breathing mode inducing dynamical pairing in Kagome materials
authors: Debmalya Chakraborty, Anushree Datta, Jorge Cayao
abstract: The breathing mode in Kagome materials is a structural modulation that breaks inversion symmetry and has been shown to be a crucial source for intriguing phases in the normal state. In this work, we carry out a full classification of superconducting symmetries in kagome superconductors and demonstrate the emergence of odd-frequency dynamical Cooper pairs entirely driven by the breathing mode. We then show that odd-frequency spin-singlet Cooper pairs can be realized by controlling the breathing mode in kagome lattices with conventional spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductivity. Since odd-frequency pairing is intrinsically nonlocal in time, our results put forward the breathing mode for designing dynamical Cooper pairs in kagome materials.
summary: This work theoretically investigates how structural distortions, specifically the 'breathing mode,' induce unconventional odd-frequency Cooper pairs in Kagome superconductors. By classifying superconducting symmetries, the authors show that this structural modulation drives a dynamical pairing mechanism even when conventional $s$-wave superconductivity is present. This establishes breathing Kagome lattices as a platform for realizing exotic, time-nonlocal quantum correlations.
main_problem: To classify superconducting symmetries in Kagome superconductors and demonstrate the emergence of odd-frequency dynamical Cooper pairs driven by structural distortions.
main_result: The breathing mode induces a specific type of odd-frequency, spin-singlet pairing ($	ext{OSEO}$ class) that can emerge even when the parent superconductivity is conventional $s$-wave.
method: Theoretical calculation involving the full classification of superconducting symmetries using anomalous Green's functions and solving the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian self-consistently.
model_or_system:
The system is based on Kagome materials, modeled with a normal state Hamiltonian that includes a structural modulation called the 'breathing mode,' which breaks inversion symmetry ($t_a 
eq t_b$).
key_observables: Superconducting pair amplitudes symmetry (even/odd under frequency/spin), odd-frequency pairing signatures, and quasiparticle interference ($\deltaho_a(q, \omega)$).
important_parameters: The structural distortion parameter ($t_a - t_b$) is crucial; superconductivity exists in specific chemical potential ranges ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially considers the simplest onsite spin-singlet superconductivity using $\Delta_{AA}, \Delta_{BB}, \Delta_{CC}$ as independent order parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures comparing pristine vs. distorted lattices, and show self-consistent superconducting order parameters ($\Delta_{\alpha\alpha'}$) dependence on chemical potential.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by classifying allowed pair symmetries based on symmetry constraints, demonstrating how the breathing mode opens gaps at Dirac points, leading to the emergence of odd-frequency pairing mechanisms.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state superconductivity, the concept of dynamical pairing driven by structural fluctuations (a form of coupling between lattice degrees of freedom and electronic correlations) is relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated systems.
